llm.summary: ClawSentry appears to install a real OpenClaw security plugin, but its installer performs high-impact authentication, device fingerprinting, credential storage, background polling, cleanup, and gateway restart actions that need careful review.

dimensions.detail: The security-plugin installation purpose is coherent, and SKILL.md discloses fingerprinting, login-token creation, local state, background monitoring, and config updates. The implementation also removes existing plugin state, writes returned API credentials, and restarts the OpenClaw gateway, which materially expands the setup authority.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs running a bundled Node script directly. Execution is user-invoked, but after launch the script automatically contacts remote APIs, starts detached login polling, mutates OpenClaw config, and restarts the gateway without separate confirmation steps.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Installation depends on an opaque bundled CommonJS script with host command execution via openclaw CLI, filesystem deletion under a configured install path, HTTPS calls, and bundled node-machine-id behavior. This is disclosed in part, but it is a broad trust mechanism for a security-sensitive installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Remote authorization and device binding are plausibly related to activating the security service, but the script sends a stable machine identifier, stores login token and fingerprint in .state/login_state.json, writes an API key into plugin config, and logs full identity responses that may include sensitive fields.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The background process is time-bounded to about 10 minutes and is disclosed, but it is detached and continues after the main script exits. The script also persists local state/logs and automatically restarts the OpenClaw gateway after successful login.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust this publisher and the Volcengine/Omni Shield service. Before running it, understand that it will execute local Node code, send a stable device fingerprint to a remote service, create and store a login token, install and reconfigure an OpenClaw plugin, store an API key in plugin configuration, write logs/state under .state, remove previous plugin installation data, and restart the OpenClaw gateway automatically.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] expected: Remote login token creation, status polling, and plugin configuration are consistent with account-based activation, but they are high-impact behaviors beyond simple installation.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact discloses several sensitive operations, but the limited-scope/security wording omits or understates plugin directory removal, gateway restart, and possible credential-bearing logs.
[SDI-2] expected: The device fingerprint is used for vendor login/device binding and is mentioned in SKILL.md, but it is a stable host identifier with limited consent, retention, and alternative-path disclosure.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Persisting login tokens/device fingerprints and logging full identity responses is not necessary to the same degree as plugin activation and increases local exposure risk.
[EA1] expected: Executing a bundled installer is central to this skill's workflow and disclosed, but it grants broad local command, filesystem, network, and process authority.
[StaticScan] expected: The static scan was clean, but manual artifact review confirms security-relevant behaviors that justify Review despite no static malicious finding.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal was pending and was not used as a basis for escalation.
